sanskrit: saṃskṛtaṃ prasavaṃ yāti vanyam annaṃ caturvidham akṣayyaṃ vardhate cānnaṃ tena bhojayate dvijān
english: The fourfold food of the forest — prepared grain, fruits, roots, and greens — goes forth abundantly; the inexhaustible food keeps multiplying, and with it the lord feeds the twice-born.

sanskrit: bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu bhojayitvānujān api śeṣaṃ vighasasaṃjñaṃ tu paścād bhuṅkte yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhojayitvā śeṣam aśnāti pārṣatī
english: When the brahmins have eaten, and the younger brothers have been fed as well, Yudhiṣṭhira eats afterwards the remnant known as vighasā; and when Yudhiṣṭhira has been fed, Draupadī, the daughter of Pṛṣata, eats whatever remains.

sanskrit: evaṃ divākarāt prāpya divākarasamadyutiḥ kāmān mano 'bhilaṣitān brāhmaṇebhyo dadau prabhuḥ
english: Thus, having received the boon from the Sun-god, the lord, himself blazing with the Sun's own radiance, bestowed upon the brahmins whatever desires and wishes of the heart they harboured.

sanskrit: purohitapurogāś ca tithinakṣatraparvasu yajñiyārthāḥ pravartante vidhimantrapramāṇataḥ
english: With the family priest at their head, on the appointed lunar days, stellar conjunctions, and festival occasions, sacrificial rites were performed in accordance with prescribed injunctions and sacred formulas.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtasvastyayanā dhaumyena saha pāṇḍavāḥ dvijasaṃghaiḥ parivṛtāḥ prayayuḥ kāmyakaṃ vanam
english: Then, having had auspicious benedictions performed by Dhaumya, the Pāṇḍavas, surrounded by hosts of twice-born, set out for the Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vanaṃ praviṣṭeṣv atha pāṇḍaveṣu; prajñācakṣus tapyamāno 'mbikeyaḥ dharmātmānaṃ viduram agādhabuddhiṃ; sukhāsīno vākyam uvāca rājā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After the Pāṇḍavas had entered the forest, Ambikā's son, who sees with the eye of wisdom yet was burning with anguish, seated at ease, addressed Vidura — that soul of dharma, of unfathomable intellect — with these words.

sanskrit: prajñā ca te bhārgavasyeva śuddhā; dharmaṃ ca tvaṃ paramaṃ vettha sūkṣmam samaś ca tvaṃ saṃmataḥ kauravāṇāṃ; pathyaṃ caiṣāṃ mama caiva bravīhi
english: Your wisdom is pure as that of Bhṛgu's line; you know dharma in its highest and most subtle form; you are esteemed as impartial among all the Kurus. Tell me, therefore, what is beneficial both for them and for me.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate vidura yad adya kāryaṃ; paurāś ceme katham asmān bhajeran te cāpy asmān noddhareyuḥ samūlān; na kāmaye tāṃś ca vinaśyamānān
english: Given that matters have come to this pass, Vidura, what should be done now? How might the citizens still take our side? And may those Pāṇḍavas not uproot us utterly — yet I do not wish to see them destroyed either.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca trivargo 'yaṃ dharmamūlo narendra; rājyaṃ cedaṃ dharmamūlaṃ vadanti dharme rājan vartamānaḥ svaśaktyā; putrān sarvān pāhi kuntīsutāṃś ca
english: Vidura said: These three aims of life, O lord of men, are rooted in dharma; and kingship, they say, is likewise rooted in dharma. Therefore, O king, abiding in dharma with all your strength, protect all your sons — and the sons of Kuntī as well.

sanskrit: sa vai dharmo vipraluptaḥ sabhāyāṃ; pāpātmabhiḥ saubaleyapradhānaiḥ āhūya kuntīsutam akṣavatyāṃ; parājaiṣīt satyasaṃdhaṃ sutas te
english: That very dharma was violated in the assembly-hall by wicked-souled men with Śakuni's son at their head: having invited the son of Kuntī to the dice-game, your son defeated him — that man of steadfast truth — by fraud.

sanskrit: etasya te duṣpraṇītasya rājañ; śeṣasyāhaṃ paripaśyāmy upāyam yathā putras tava kauravya pāpān; mukto loke pratitiṣṭheta sādhu
english: For this wrong course of yours, O king, I see a remedy for what remains, whereby your son, O descendant of the Kurus, freed from his sins, may stand well-regarded in the world.

sanskrit: tad vai sarvaṃ pāṇḍuputrā labhantāṃ; yat tad rājann atisṛṣṭaṃ tvayāsīt eṣa dharmaḥ paramo yat svakena; rājā tuṣyen na parasveṣu gṛdhyet
english: Let the sons of Pāṇḍu receive back all that was once given away by you, O king. This is the highest dharma: that a king should be content with his own and should not covet what belongs to others.

sanskrit: etat kāryaṃ tava sarvapradhānaṃ; teṣāṃ tuṣṭiḥ śakuneś cāvamānaḥ evaṃ śeṣaṃ yadi putreṣu te syād; etad rājaṃs tvaramāṇaḥ kuruṣva
english: This is the foremost of all duties before you: their satisfaction and the humbling of Śakuni. If such an outcome among your sons is still possible, then act upon this without delay, O king.

sanskrit: athaitad evaṃ na karoṣi rājan; dhruvaṃ kurūṇāṃ bhavitā vināśaḥ na hi kruddho bhīmaseno 'rjuno vā; śeṣaṃ kuryāc chātravāṇām anīke
english: But if you do not act thus, O king, the destruction of the Kurus is certain; for when Bhīmasena or Arjuna is enraged, he will leave no remnant of the enemy's army on the field.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ yoddhā savyasācī kṛtāstro; dhanur yeṣāṃ gāṇḍivaṃ lokasāram yeṣāṃ bhīmo bāhuśālī ca yoddhā; teṣāṃ loke kiṃ nu na prāpyam asti
english: Among those whose warrior is the ambidextrous Savyasācī, master of arms; whose bow is the Gāṇḍīva, the essence of the world; and whose fighter is the mighty-armed Bhīma — what in this world is beyond their reach?

sanskrit: uktaṃ pūrvaṃ jātamātre sute te; mayā yat te hitam āsīt tadānīm putraṃ tyajemam ahitaṃ kulasyety; etad rājan na ca tat tvaṃ cakartha idānīṃ te hitam uktaṃ na cet tvaṃ; kartāsi rājan paritaptāsi paścāt
english: It was said by me even before, the moment your son was born — what was beneficial then: 'Abandon this child, who shall bring ruin to the family.' That, O king, you did not do. Now again beneficial counsel is given to you; if you do not act upon it, O king, you shall grieve hereafter.

sanskrit: yady etad evam anumantā sutas te; saṃprīyamāṇaḥ pāṇḍavair ekarājyam tāpo na te vai bhavitā prītiyogāt; tvaṃ cen na gṛhṇāsi sutaṃ sahāyaiḥ athāparo bhavati hi taṃ nigṛhya; pāṇḍoḥ putraṃ prakuruṣvādhipatye
english: If your son consents to this and is reconciled with the Pāṇḍavas in a single undivided kingdom, there will be no sorrow for you — joy will prevail. But if you do not restrain your son and his allies, then let another arise who, having curbed him, shall install the son of Pāṇḍu as sovereign.

sanskrit: ajātaśatrur hi vimuktarāgo; dharmeṇemāṃ pṛthivīṃ śāstu rājan tato rājan pārthivāḥ sarva eva; vaiśyā ivāsmān upatiṣṭhantu sadyaḥ
english: Let Ajātaśatru, free from passion, rule this earth by dharma, O king; then, O king, all earthly rulers will immediately attend upon us like merchants seeking a patron.

sanskrit: duryodhanaḥ śakuniḥ sūtaputraḥ; prītyā rājan pāṇḍuputrān bhajantām duḥśāsano yācatu bhīmasenaṃ; sabhāmadhye drupadasyātmajāṃ ca
english: Let Duryodhana, Śakuni, and the son of the charioteer approach the sons of Pāṇḍu with good will, O king; and let Duḥśāsana entreat Bhīmasena and the daughter of Drupada in the midst of the assembly-hall.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tvaṃ parisāntvayasva; rājye cainaṃ sthāpayasvābhipūjya tvayā pṛṣṭaḥ kim aham anyad vadeyam; etat kṛtvā kṛtakṛtyo 'si rājan
english: Pacify Yudhiṣṭhira yourself, and restore him to the kingdom with full honour. What more could I say when asked by you? Having done this, you will have accomplished everything, O king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca etad vākyaṃ vidura yat te sabhāyām; iha proktaṃ pāṇḍavān prāpya māṃ ca hitaṃ teṣām ahitaṃ māmakānām; etat sarvaṃ mama nopaiti cetaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: These words of yours, Vidura, spoken in the assembly-hall and spoken here in my presence — words beneficial to the Pāṇḍavas and harmful to my own — none of this enters my heart.

sanskrit: idaṃ tv idānīṃ kuta eva niścitaṃ; teṣām arthe pāṇḍavānāṃ yad āttha tenādya manye nāsi hito mameti; kathaṃ hi putraṃ pāṇḍavārthe tyajeyam
english: And how is it so resolutely decided now, this thing you advocate on behalf of the Pāṇḍavas? By this I now think you are no friend of mine. For how can I abandon my son for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ te 'pi mamaiva putrā; duryodhanas tu mama dehāt prasūtaḥ svaṃ vai dehaṃ parahetos tyajeti; ko nu brūyāt samatām anvavekṣan
english: Doubtless the Pāṇḍavas too are sons to me; yet Duryodhana was born from my own body. Who, looking at the matter impartially, would say: 'Abandon your own body for the sake of another'?

sanskrit: sa mā jihmaṃ vidura sarvaṃ bravīṣi; mānaṃ ca te 'ham adhikaṃ dhārayāmi yathecchakaṃ gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā tvaṃ; susāntvyamānāpy asatī strī jahāti
english: You speak to me nothing but crooked counsel, Vidura; yet I still hold you in the highest regard. Go wherever you wish or stay — even a wicked woman, though well-soothed, will abandon her husband.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāvad uktvā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'nvapadyad; antarveśma sahasotthāya rājan nedam astīty atha viduro bhāṣamāṇaḥ; saṃprādravad yatra pārthā babhūvuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Dhṛtarāṣṭra abruptly rose and retreated into his inner apartments, O king. Then Vidura, still speaking — 'This is not right!' — ran swiftly to where the sons of Pṛthā were.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pāṇḍavās tu vane vāsam uddiśya bharatarṣabhāḥ prayayur jāhnavīkūlāt kurukṣetraṃ sahānugāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The Pāṇḍavas, bulls among the Bhāratas, set out from the bank of the Jāhnavī toward Kurukṣetra, intending to dwell in the forest, together with their followers.

sanskrit: sarasvatīdṛṣadvatyau yamunāṃ ca niṣevya te yayur vanenaiva vanaṃ satataṃ paścimāṃ diśam
english: After sojourning at the Sarasvatī and Dṛṣadvatī rivers and at the Yamunā, they journeyed continually through forest after forest toward the western direction.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarasvatīkūle sameṣu marudhanvasu kāmyakaṃ nāma dadṛśur vanaṃ munijanapriyam
english: Then, on the level sandy plains along the Sarasvatī bank, they came upon a forest called Kāmyaka, beloved of sages.

sanskrit: tatra te nyavasan vīrā vane bahumṛgadvije anvāsyamānā munibhiḥ sāntvyamānāś ca bhārata
english: There those heroes dwelt in that forest teeming with deer and birds, waited upon by sages and comforted by them, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: viduras tv api pāṇḍūnāṃ tadā darśanalālasaḥ jagāmaikarathenaiva kāmyakaṃ vanam ṛddhimat
english: Vidura too, burning with longing to see the Pāṇḍavas, then went with a single chariot to the prosperous Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: tato yātvā viduraḥ kānanaṃ tac; chīghrair aśvair vāhinā syandanena dadarśāsīnaṃ dharmarājaṃ vivikte; sārdhaṃ draupadyā bhrātṛbhir brāhmaṇaiś ca
english: Having driven swiftly to that forest with fleet horses drawing his chariot, Vidura saw the King of Dharma seated in a secluded spot, together with Draupadī, his brothers, and the brahmins.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyad viduraṃ tūrṇam ārād; abhyāyāntaṃ satyasaṃdhaḥ sa rājā athābravīd bhrātaraṃ bhīmasenaṃ; kiṃ nu kṣattā vakṣyati naḥ sametya
english: Then that king of steadfast truth caught sight of Vidura approaching swiftly from afar, and said to his brother Bhīmasena: 'What will Kṣattā have to say to us when he arrives?'

sanskrit: kaccin nāyaṃ vacanāt saubalasya; samāhvātā devanāyopayāti kaccit kṣudraḥ śakunir nāyudhāni; jeṣyaty asmān punar evākṣavatyām
english: 'Perhaps he comes summoned at the word of Śakuni's son, bearing a challenge? Could that vile Śakuni be coming again to defeat us with weapons, or once more at the dice-board?'

sanskrit: samāhūtaḥ kena cid ādraveti; nāhaṃ śakto bhīmasenāpayātum gāṇḍīve vā saṃśayite kathaṃ cid; rājyaprāptiḥ saṃśayitā bhaven naḥ
english: 'Summoned by someone, I cannot in any case withdraw from Bhīmasena's side; nor can I in any way set the Gāṇḍīva bow aside — for that would make our recovery of the kingdom doubtful.'

sanskrit: tata utthāya viduraṃ pāṇḍaveyāḥ; pratyagṛhṇan nṛpate sarva eva taiḥ satkṛtaḥ sa ca tān ājamīḍho; yathocitaṃ pāṇḍuputrān sameyāt
english: Then, rising up, all the sons of Pāṇḍu received Vidura with due respect, O king. Honoured by them, that descendant of Ajamīḍha in turn greeted the sons of Pāṇḍu as was fitting.

sanskrit: samāśvastaṃ viduraṃ te nararṣabhās; tato 'pṛcchann āgamanāya hetum sa cāpi tebhyo vistarataḥ śaśaṃsa; yathāvṛtto dhṛtarāṣṭro ''mbikeyaḥ
english: When Vidura had been set at ease, those bulls among men then asked him the reason for his coming; and he in turn told them in full detail how Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, had behaved.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca avocan māṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'nuguptam; ajātaśatro parigṛhyābhipūjya evaṃ gate samatām abhyupetya; pathyaṃ teṣāṃ mama caiva bravīhi
english: Vidura said: Dhṛtarāṣṭra took me aside in private, O Ajātaśatru, and having honoured me warmly, said: 'Given that things have come to this pass, and seeing them as equal to me, tell me what is beneficial for them and for me as well.'

sanskrit: mayāpy uktaṃ yat kṣamaṃ kauravāṇāṃ; hitaṃ pathyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya caiva tad vai pathyaṃ tan mano nābhyupaiti; tataś cāhaṃ kṣamam anyan na manye
english: I too spoke what was wholesome and beneficial for the Kurus and for Dhṛtarāṣṭra himself. But that wholesome counsel did not enter his heart; and therefore I do not see any other course as fitting.

sanskrit: paraṃ śreyaḥ pāṇḍaveyā mayoktaṃ; na me tac ca śrutavān āmbikeyaḥ yathāturasyeva hi pathyam annaṃ; na rocate smāsya tad ucyamānam
english: The highest good was spoken by me to you, O sons of Pāṇḍu; yet Ambikā's son would not hear it from me. Just as a sick man has no relish for wholesome food, so that counsel, however beneficial, did not please him when it was uttered.

sanskrit: na śreyase nīyate 'jātaśatro; strī śrotriyasyeva gṛhe praduṣṭā bruvan na rucyai bharatarṣabhasya; patiḥ kumāryā iva ṣaṣṭivarṣaḥ
english: He is not led toward what is good, O Ajātaśatru — like a corrupt woman in a brahmin's household. My words found no favour with that bull among Bhāratas, just as a husband of sixty finds no favour with a young maiden.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ vināśo nṛpa kauravāṇāṃ; na vai śreyo dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ paraiti yathā parṇe puṣkarasyeva siktaṃ; jalaṃ na tiṣṭhet pathyam uktaṃ tathāsmin
english: The destruction of the Kurus is certain, O king; Dhṛtarāṣṭra does not pursue what is truly good. Just as water poured on a lotus leaf does not stay, so beneficial counsel, once spoken, does not remain in him.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīn māṃ; yatra śraddhā bhārata tatra yāhi nāhaṃ bhūyaḥ kāmaye tvāṃ sahāyaṃ; mahīm imāṃ pālayituṃ puraṃ vā
english: Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra, angered, said to me: 'Go wherever you please, O Bhārata. I no longer desire your help in governing this earth or this city.'

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tyakto dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājaṃs; tvāṃ śāsitum upayātas tvarāvān tad vai sarvaṃ yan mayoktaṃ sabhāyāṃ; tad dhāryatāṃ yat pravakṣyāmi bhūyaḥ
english: So I, dismissed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O king, have hastened here to counsel you. Hold firm in all that I spoke in the assembly-hall; and now hear further what I shall say.

sanskrit: kleśais tīvrair yujyamānaḥ sapatnaiḥ; kṣamāṃ kurvan kālam upāsate yaḥ saṃ vardhayan stokam ivāgnim ātmavān; sa vai bhuṅkte pṛthivīm eka eva
english: He who, though afflicted by harsh sufferings at the hands of enemies, practices forbearance and bides his time — nurturing himself like a small flame being fed to grow — that self-possessed man alone shall in the end enjoy the entire earth.

sanskrit: yasyāvibhaktaṃ vasu rājan sahāyais; tasya duḥkhe 'py aṃśabhājaḥ sahāyāḥ sahāyānām eṣa saṃgrahaṇe 'bhyupāyaḥ; sahāyāptau pṛthivīprāptim āhuḥ
english: He whose resources are shared undivided with his allies — those allies will be sharers in his suffering as well. This is the means of retaining allies: through shared fortune. And in the gaining of allies, they say, lies the gaining of the earth.

sanskrit: satyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ pāṇḍava niṣpralāpaṃ; tulyaṃ cānnaṃ saha bhojyaṃ sahāyaiḥ ātmā caiṣām agrato nātivarted; evaṃvṛttir vardhate bhūmipālaḥ
english: Truth is supreme, O Pāṇḍava — truth without empty speech; and food shared equally and eaten together with allies; and let a king never overstep himself before them. A ruler who lives in this way shall prosper.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā bravīṣi; parāṃ buddhim upagamyāpramattaḥ yac cāpy anyad deśakālopapannaṃ; tad vai vācyaṃ tat kariṣyāmi kṛtsnam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I shall act exactly as you counsel, bringing the highest understanding to bear, without carelessness. And whatever else is appropriate to time and place — that too you must tell me, and I shall carry it all out in full.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gate tu vidure rājann āśramaṃ pāṇḍavān prati dhṛtarāṣṭro mahāprājñaḥ paryatapyata bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But after Vidura had gone to the hermitage to the Pāṇḍavas, O king, the greatly wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra was tormented with anguish, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa sabhādvāram āgamya vidurasmāramohitaḥ samakṣaṃ pārthivendrāṇāṃ papātāviṣṭacetanaḥ
english: Coming to the entrance of the assembly-hall, overcome with the grief of remembering Vidura, his senses overwhelmed, he fell down before the assembled kings.

sanskrit: sa tu labdhvā punaḥ saṃjñāṃ samutthāya mahītalāt samīpopasthitaṃ rājā saṃjayaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Regaining consciousness, he rose from the earth, and the king addressed Saṃjaya, who was standing close by, with these words.

sanskrit: bhrātā mama suhṛc caiva sākṣād dharma ivāparaḥ tasya smṛtvādya subhṛśaṃ hṛdayaṃ dīryatīva me
english: 'My brother and my friend — verily a second Dharma made manifest — thinking of him now, my heart is riven asunder.

sanskrit: tam ānayasva dharmajñaṃ mama bhrātaram āśu vai iti bruvan sa nṛpatiḥ karuṇaṃ paryadevayat
english: Bring back to me quickly that knower of dharma, my brother!' — saying this, the king lamented piteously.

sanskrit: paścāttāpābhisaṃtapto vidurasmārakarśitaḥ bhrātṛsnehād idaṃ rājan saṃjayaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Consumed by remorse, tormented by the remembrance of Vidura, out of love for his brother, O king, he spoke these words to Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: gaccha saṃjaya jānīhi bhrātaraṃ viduraṃ mama yadi jīvati roṣeṇa mayā pāpena nirdhutaḥ
english: 'Go, Saṃjaya, and find out whether my brother Vidura still lives, he who was driven away in anger by me, a sinner.

sanskrit: na hi tena mama bhrātrā susūkṣmam api kiṃ cana vyalīkaṃ kṛtapūrvaṃ me prājñenāmitabuddhinā
english: For that wise brother of mine, of boundless intellect, has never done me the slightest wrong, not even the most minute offense.

sanskrit: sa vyalīkaṃ kathaṃ prāpto mattaḥ paramabuddhimān na jahyāj jīvitaṃ prājñas taṃ gacchānaya saṃjaya
english: How has that supremely wise man received such injury from me? A wise man would not abandon his life for this. Go, Saṃjaya, bring him to me.'

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājñas tam anumānya ca saṃjayo bāḍham ity uktvā prādravat kāmyakaṃ vanam
english: Having heard the king's words and taken his leave, Saṃjaya said 'So be it' and ran swiftly to the Kāmyaka forest.

sanskrit: so 'cireṇa samāsādya tad vanaṃ yatra pāṇḍavāḥ rauravājinasaṃvītaṃ dadarśātha yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Reaching that forest without delay, where the Pāṇḍavas were, he then saw Yudhiṣṭhira clad in the hide of the ruru deer.

sanskrit: vidureṇa sahāsīnaṃ brāhmaṇaiś ca sahasraśaḥ bhrātṛbhiś cābhisaṃguptaṃ devair iva śatakratum
english: He was seated with Vidura and with thousands of brahmins, guarded by his brothers — like Indra of a hundred sacrifices attended by the gods.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiram athābhyetya pūjayām āsa saṃjayaḥ bhīmārjunayamāṃś cāpi tadarhaṃ pratyapadyata
english: Approaching Yudhiṣṭhira, Saṃjaya paid him homage; and he also rendered appropriate honour to Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins.

sanskrit: rājñā pṛṣṭaḥ sa kuśalaṃ sukhāsīnaś ca saṃjayaḥ śaśaṃsāgamane hetum idaṃ caivābravīd vacaḥ
english: Questioned by the king about his well-being and seated comfortably, Saṃjaya told him the reason for his coming and spoke these words.

sanskrit: rājā smarati te kṣattar dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ taṃ paśya gatvā tvaṃ kṣipraṃ saṃjīvaya ca pārthivam
english: 'King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, remembers you, O Kṣattā. Go quickly to see him and revive the king's spirit.'

sanskrit: so 'numānya naraśreṣṭhān pāṇḍavān kurunandanān niyogād rājasiṃhasya gantum arhasi mānada
english: 'Having taken leave of the best of men, the Pāṇḍavas, those joys of the Kuru line, you should go at the command of that lion among kings, O giver of honour.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu viduro dhīmān svajanavatsalaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasyānumate punar āyād gajāhvayam
english: Thus addressed, the wise Vidura, who was affectionate to his own people, with Yudhiṣṭhira's consent, returned again to Gajāhvaya — the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahāprājñaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pratāpavān diṣṭyā prāpto 'si dharmajña diṣṭyā smarasi me 'nagha
english: The powerful Dhṛtarāṣṭra addressed that man of great wisdom: 'By good fortune you have arrived, O knower of dharma; by good fortune you remember me, O sinless one.'

sanskrit: adya rātrau divā cāhaṃ tvatkṛte bharatarṣabha prajāgare prapaśyāmi vicitraṃ deham ātmanaḥ
english: 'This night past and during the day, because of you, O bull of the Bhāratas, I lay awake and saw strange visions of my own body.'

sanskrit: so 'ṅkam ādāya viduraṃ mūrdhny upāghrāya caiva ha kṣamyatām iti covāca yad ukto 'si mayā ruṣā
english: Taking Vidura upon his lap and smelling his head in welcome, he said: 'Let it be forgiven — all that was said to you by me in anger.'

sanskrit: vidura uvāca kṣāntam eva mayā rājan gurur naḥ paramo bhavān tathā hy asmy āgataḥ kṣipraṃ tvaddarśanaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Vidura said: It is already forgiven by me, O king; you are our supreme elder and guru. That is precisely why I have come back quickly, intent on seeing you.

sanskrit: bhavanti hi naravyāghra puruṣā dharmacetasaḥ dīnābhipātino rājan nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: For there are men, O tiger among men, whose hearts are rooted in dharma and who rush to the aid of the distressed, O king — in this there should be no deliberation.

sanskrit: pāṇḍoḥ sutā yādṛśā me tādṛśā me sutās tava dīnā iti hi me buddhir abhipannādya tān prati
english: The sons of Pāṇḍu are to me as your sons are to me; and it is with the thought 'they are suffering' that my mind has turned to them now.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca anyonyam anunīyaivaṃ bhrātarau tau mahādyutī viduro dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca lebhāte paramāṃ mudam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus appeased each other in this way, those two brothers of great splendour — Vidura and Dhṛtarāṣṭra — experienced the greatest joy.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā ca viduraṃ prāptaṃ rājñā ca parisāntvitam dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajo rājā paryatapyata durmatiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that Vidura had returned and been mollified by the king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son — that evil-minded king — was consumed with anguish.

sanskrit: sa saubalaṃ samānāyya karṇaduḥśāsanāv api abravīd vacanaṃ rājā praviśyābuddhijaṃ tamaḥ
english: Having summoned Śakuni, Karṇa, and Duḥśāsana, the king, entering the darkness born of folly, spoke these words.

sanskrit: eṣa pratyāgato mantrī dhṛtarāṣṭrasya saṃmataḥ viduraḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ suhṛd vidvān hite rataḥ
english: 'This Vidura, the trusted counsellor of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, has returned — the learned friend of the sons of Pāṇḍu, ever devoted to their welfare.

sanskrit: yāvad asya punar buddhiṃ viduro nāpakarṣati pāṇḍavānayane tāvan mantrayadhvaṃ hitaṃ mama
english: 'Before Vidura can once again turn the king's mind in the direction of bringing back the Pāṇḍavas, deliberate quickly on what is beneficial for me.'

sanskrit: atha paśyāmy ahaṃ pārthān prāptān iha kathaṃ cana punaḥ śoṣaṃ gamiṣyāmi nirāsur niravagrahaḥ
english: 'If I should ever see the sons of Pṛthā arrive here again, I shall waste away once more — without hope, without support.

sanskrit: viṣam udbandhanaṃ vāpi śastram agnipraveśanam kariṣye na hi tān ṛddhān punar draṣṭum ihotsahe
english: 'I would take poison, hang myself, seize a weapon, or walk into fire — I cannot bring myself to see those prosperous ones again in this world.'

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca kiṃ bāliṣāṃ matiṃ rājann āsthito 'si viśāṃ pate gatās te samayaṃ kṛtvā naitad evaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Śakuni said: 'Why do you entertain such childish thoughts, O king, O lord of men? They have gone after entering into an agreement — this will not come to pass as you fear.'

sanskrit: satyavākye sthitāḥ sarve pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha pitus te vacanaṃ tāta na grahīṣyanti karhi cit
english: 'All the Pāṇḍavas are bound to their word of truth, O bull of the Bhāratas; your father's command, dear one, they will never accept under any circumstances.'

sanskrit: atha vā te grahīṣyanti punar eṣyanti vā puram nirasya samayaṃ bhūyaḥ paṇo 'smākaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: 'Or if they do accept it and return to the city, then, discarding the agreement, we shall have another round of the wager.'
